post.description: Run a single command with action=shell and command=<shell text> when enabled, or a fixed action, in an explicitly opted-in development Pod through the private Kubernetes MCP Server. Actions: redis_ping, nginx_check, disk_usage, process_list, environment, read_file, process_status, memory_usage. read_file requires an exact administrator-approved path; process_status accepts a numeric PID. Shell uses /bin/sh -c inside the target container and the configured interceptor; no interactive stdin or TTY. Returns upstream text, not separate streams or an exit code. Timeout may leave the remote process running; do not blindly retry.

post.description: Single-use authenticated download. Errors after headers abort the stream. Range unsupported.

Prepare a single-use downloadId and HTTP POST downloadUrl, valid for five minutes and bound to the authenticated user and Pod UID. Use curl with the same Bearer credential and JSON {downloadId:...}, saving the binary response locally. No file bytes in MCP. No fixed size limit or resume. Container requires tar. ConfigMap symlinks are followed. Relative URLs use the same service and gateway prefix as this MCP.

Prepare a five-minute, single-use uploadId/uploadUrl bound to your user and Pod UID. HTTP POST raw file bytes with the same Bearer credential and X-Upload-Id header; curl --data-binary @local-file with Content-Length (chunked uploads unsupported). Creates one new 0600 file in an existing writable directory; never overwrites. No fixed size limit, resume, directory upload or automatic reload. Container needs /bin/sh, head (-c), wc, sha256sum, mkdir, rmdir, rm, ln. Commit only after complete transfer and remote size/SHA-256 verification. No file bytes in MCP.
Requires Content-Length; chunked and resume unsupported. One new file, never overwrite. No application size cap.
Get bounded Pod container logs (no streaming). Logs may contain application-sensitive data
Close your session and release its connection. Can close after Pod deletion; remote process termination is not guaranteed.
Start a user-owned /bin/sh session. Optional tty=true merges streams; open means stream starting, read state to detect failure. Not SSH. Sessions expire and do not survive server restart.
Read up to 64 KiB of binary-safe outputBase64 with a byte cursor; waitSeconds 0-5. lostBytes reports overwritten ring-buffer data. Streams merged; ANSI terminal sequences retained.
Send input to your terminal; include newline to execute. Input may be control characters such as U+0003 for Ctrl+C (TTY required). Sent is not confirmation of remote process termination.
